strengths: Clean controlled experimental design with three matched-compute conditions that directly isolates the variable of interest (draft quality vs. two-stage structure)
Counterintuitive and actionable finding: worst-of-formatted selection outperforms best-of-N, which challenges the intuitive assumption and has practical implications for training efficiency
Provides a mechanistic hypothesis (50% more gradient-active training groups) that is quantifiable and points toward future work
Reports confidence intervals on the recovery ratio, showing basic statistical rigor
weaknesses: Scope is very narrow — the paper is essentially a single ablation on a single method (iGRPO) on a single benchmark (MATH500), which limits generalizability
The mechanistic explanation (gradient-active training groups) is correlational, not causal; no intervention is performed to confirm this is the actual driver of performance
Only one benchmark is reported in the abstract; broader evaluation across diverse reasoning tasks would substantially strengthen the claim
The 'worst-of-formatted' condition confounds two factors — draft quality and draft format — making it unclear whether formatting alone drives the result
The contributions section largely restates the abstract findings verbatim rather than contextualizing the broader implications for RL training of LLMs

ai_detection.reasoning: The introduction exhibits a dense cluster of canonical AI-writing signals: a rigid three-part numbered contributions list that mirrors the abstract almost verbatim, formulaic transition phrases ('a surprising finding', 'our contributions are threefold'), a single-thread linear narrative anchored to one prior method, and uniform sentence cadence throughout. The prose lacks the stylistic variation, hedging nuance, and contextual digression typical of human academic writing.
